key_insight: Binary success rates hide critical failure modes in fine-grained manipulation; MetaFine is a diagnostic meta-evaluation framework that decomposes manipulation performance into interpretable, component-level metrics and reveals up to 70% inflation in reported capabilities.
problem_solved: Current embodied-AI benchmarks reduce complex manipulation tasks to a single pass/fail score, masking failures in local attribute grounding, spatial perception, and constraint-respecting execution and preventing targeted improvement and safe deployment.
method: Define a compact suite of fine-grained diagnostic metrics (e.g., attribute grounding accuracy, spatial alignment error, constraint violation rate) to replace/augment binary success.
Apply systematic perturbations and targeted probes in simulated and real testbeds to isolate which sub-capacities (perception, grounding, control) cause failures.
Aggregate component-level scores into a meta-evaluation report (visualizations + quantitative inflation estimate) that identifies architectural bottlenecks.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to quantify where manipulation systems actually fail, enabling targeted model/robot improvements, more reliable benchmarking, and safer real-world deployment.

paper_title: Beyond Binary Success: A Diagnostic Meta-Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Manipulation
paper_authors: He-Yang Xu, Pengyuan Zhang, Zongyuan Ge, Xiaoshuai Hao, Serge Belongie
